description: Cluster I is the largest cluster with 181 articles, crediting about 40% of the (2134) citations to KMRP. The central focus of the group is on ‘knowledge sharing’ (Bosua & Scheepers, 2007; Lin, 2006; Yi, 2009) along with other concepts like ‘knowledge transfer’ (Frank & Ribeiro, 2014; Riss et al., 2007), ‘knowledge exchange’ (Scarso & Bolisani, 2012), ‘trust and organisational support’ (Burnett et al., 2015; Michailova & Sidorova, 2011). Usoro et al. (2007) is the most cited article in the cluster with 135 citations. The article suggests that the three components of trust (competence, integrity and benevolence) are positively related to knowledge sharing. Yi (2009) contributed a scale for ‘knowledge sharing behaviour’ with necessary reliability and validity. The cluster comprises of prominent conceptual studies.

Articles under cluster II dominantly discuss knowledge management (Baskerville & Dulipovici, 2006; Begoña Lloria, 2008; Mingers, 2008), tactic knowledge (Gourlay, 2006), codification (Dixon et al., 2009) and innovation (Asimakou, 2009; Kang, 2016). It comprises of 130 articles crediting 1510 citations to the journal. The most influential article of this cluster is ‘The theoretical foundations of knowledge management’ (Baskerville & Dulipovici, 2006) by Baskerville, R., and Dulipovici, A with 178 citations. The article, through an in-depth analysis of the theoretical foundations of knowledge management, established that knowledge management is a maturing arena of study. Begoña Lloria (2008) is a review paper which assembles the literature available on knowledge management and creation. This shows us that KMRP has contributed plenty of theoretical work to its concerned subject area.

The cluster comprises of 106 articles and 889 citations. The central focus of the cluster is around the various forms of capital related to knowledge management. It includes, intellectual capital (Kianto et al., 2013; Kong & Thomson, 2009; Veltri et al., 2014), knowledge asset (Massa & Testa, 2009; Moustaghfir, 2009; Schiuma, 2009), social capital (Kianto & Waajakoski, 2010; Van Reijsen et al., 2015), and relational capital (García & Bounfour, 2014; Zaragoza-Sáez & ClaverCortés, 2011). Kong and Thomson (2009) is the most influential article of the cluster with 57 citations. The article provides a holistic overview along with a theoretical framework to explain connections between intellectual capital, human resource management and strategic human resource management.

Cluster IV is the smallest cluster covering 84 articles. Around 61% of the articles of this cluster are published post-2015 which shows that the themes covered under it are relatively recent. The primary concentration of the group is on social networking (Díez-Vial & Montoro-Sánchez, 2014; Kang & Kim, 2017; Park et al., 2017), networked innovation (Valkokari et al., 2012), collaboration (Ashyrov et al., 2019; BerbegalMirabent et al., 2019; Calvo et al., 2019), logistics (Lee & Song, 2018), absorptive capacity (Noblet et al., 2011), supply chain (Marra et al., 2016), and taxonomy (Gonzalez, 2017). ‘Enhancing knowledge transfer in multinational corporations: a dynamic capabilities driven model’ (2007) is the most cited article of the cluster with 45 citations. Noblet et al. (2011) studied innovative small and medium enterprises and established that strong absorptive and innovative capacity is carried by the most open firms.
